newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Danu Bank, Finance One sign merger pact.
newsitem.headline: Thai Danu Bank, Finance One sign merger pact.

text.p: Thailand's largest finance firm, Finance One Plc and medium-sized Thai Danu Bank Plc on Friday signed a memorandum of understanding agreeing to merge.
The biggest merger of Thai financial institutions would create a new entity called Thai Danu Bank which would be granted a new commercial bank licence, the Bank of Thailand said.
The merger will upgrade Thai Danu Bank to the ninth largest bank in the country from 12th previously and give it universal banking capabilities.

President of Finance One, Pin Chakapak, and Pornsanong Tuchinda, president of Thai Danu, signed the memorandum in the presence of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan and central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond.
Pin said the exchange or swap ratio of shares between the two merging entities and the newly merged entity would be determined within 30 days.
The allocation, evaluation and total number of shares of the new Thai Danu Bank would be determined by market value and/or true assets value.

Pornsanong said the merger received full support from the government including a favourable tax scheme and liquidity support and all privileges currently held by Finance One would also be transfered to the newly merged entity.
"It demonstrates to both domestic and international financial market that this merger serves as a benchmark for more mergers to come," he said.
"This merger will benefit the new Thai Danu Bank as it will allow the company to take a big leap forward with quality," he said.

"Moreover, Finance One's rights and privileges would be transferred to the new bank enabling it to offer universal banking services, provide it with more human resources and enable it to cut costs," he said.
The announcement of the merger between the two financial institutions early in the month preceded a major shake up of Thailand's troubled finance sector.
Analysts had said that Finance One sought the merger because it faced liquidity problems. Its woes were symptomatic of major cash flow problems faced by many finance companies.

Last week, the Thai authorities ordered 10 weakened finance firms to raise their capital and told banks and finance companies to raise their provisioning for sub-standard loans, given mainly to the depressed property sector.
The revamp sent shock waves through the financial system causing the stock market and prices of bank and finance firms to initially tumble.

The stock exchange said in a statement late on Friday that the shares of Finance One and Thai Danu bank would remain suspended and there would be no lifting of the ban on trading as rumoured in the market.
The companies' shares were suspended by the bourse on March 3 when the two institutions said they were planning to merge.
